title: The privacy assistant Ollie shuts down on 6 November
friendlyTitle: The privacy assistant Ollie shuts down on 6 November
summary: Ollie co-founder Bill Lennon said on 30 October that the app will shut down on 6 November. Ollie was a subscription assistant for family organisation, connected to email and calendar, with plans for bookings, meal planning, and bills. It had raised a $7.5 million seed round led by Khosla Ventures, announced in September, and was one of the early assistants in this category to complete a SOC 2 audit. Lennon said the company could not keep up as Muse, Instinct, and others entered.
friendlySummary: Ollie's co-founder, Bill Lennon, said on 30 October that the app will shut down on 6 November. Ollie was a paid assistant for keeping a family organised. It connected to email and calendar, and planned to help with bookings, meals, and bills. It had raised $7.5 million in September and had passed a SOC 2 privacy audit, an outside check of how a company handles data. Lennon said it could not keep up after larger assistants such as Muse and Instinct entered.
whyItMatters: If you use Ollie, the next few days are for export and refunds. Lennon said customers will get those instructions. The shutdown is a reminder that a privacy audit does not keep a small assistant alive once larger agents occupy the same text-message slot. If your family workflow sits inside Ollie, move the calendar and email connections before 6 November. After that date, TechCrunch's report does not say the service remains available.
